I've been excited to announce this for a few weeks now...

@lolo_IRL will be the official networking and agenda platform for Boston Blockchain Week.

At a conference, everyone wants to know 2 things:

> who's here?
> where do I go?

Lolo solves this.

Lolo's purpose is to help people connect IRL, and for that, context matters. One of the strongest signals of context is someone's profession – in the case of @blockchainwk, everyone attending will relate on crypto, tech, and finance. 

This creates a perfect environment of network density in which everyone there is aligned, and will likely want to accomplish comparable goals and go to similar events.

Lolo provides a single, easy platform to accomplish all of that.

No more jumping around 5 telegram group chats, sending RSVP links and asking on X "who's in Boston?".
Lolo fixes it.

And afterward, everyone who went to BBW can stay connected for the future. On Lolo, your global network grows and compounds with every new connection and event, meaning you'll have people you already know at that next conference, and the one after that.

I'm looking forward to taking on this mission for Lolo, providing a platform and product which upgrades Boston Blockchain Week overall.

Ready to sink our teeth in and show what we can do, Sep. 8 - 10 in Quincy, MA.

Let's gooo. 😁🦾

candidates.text:
the future is HTML. your idea, let me touch it. HTML content is all i want to see. your deck, let me tweak some parameters in it. your website, let me fork it. your data, give me a dashboard. your idea, let me touch it. HTML your tweet. your blog. your concept. your company. everything is a website with HTML: russian dolls for content that can be endlessly looped and layered and it is all i want you to send me. the future is me saying something and granola listening and then you saying something and granola listening and instead of a silly little word doc we are going to get an HTML at the end that is a dashboard of our conversation with little next steps and visualizations and highlights and we are going to be dashboarding like crazy. this is neither good nor bad, it just will be. the future of you playing something on your phone is to tell your little agent to spin up an app to help you track your health and it will spin up a little HTML app that will disrupt any health app that is out today. did you know that you can go to your LLM right now and ask it to create you a version of flappy bird in HTML and you can just sit there and play flappy bird. and brick breaker. and chess. and you can tell it to make the colors neon or to make the bricks bubbles or to make the bird a panda. HTML everything. it is the endless app store. the future of content is a sick new way to design or write or build a website and that to be posted somewhere and then you telling your agent to mimic that but fork it in a certain way to better suit your content. cathedral essays: ideas shaped into paragraphs overlaying interactive widgets that take the concepts described in words and bring them to life. miniature museums, but inside a blog, this is the future. launches that are just websites again -- your hype video can be grokked or clauded in minutes and i don't listen to anything with sound anymore, so what's the point. HTML contains multitudes of content -- sound, movement, text. it is the most sensual of digital experiences. maybe the only thing that can grab my attention right now is a beautiful website curated for the human. if we HTML everything, this might somehow maybe be the solution to the reactive nature of scrolling. you scroll and you never engage, you never think. there is nothing active on the internet: it is endless TV: everything is tv. just as markets are for taking risk and hedging risk so that any market, taken to an extreme, becomes a battleground for high frequency traders, then social feeds are for sending information and receiving information. therefore any social feed, taken to an extreme, becomes a battleground for advertising. and because of these truths, markets beget risk taking for market maker's sake and social feeds beget scrolling for advertising's sake and hence we live in a world of advertisers and traders. HTML is the language of the LLM and the new MP3 and PNG and MP4 all wrapped into one designed for LLMs and humans and other humans to network seamlessly in the shared underwritten task of elucidating upon ideas. HTML might be the savior -- the thing that makes the internet feel less dead. and video is dead--check your instagram feed and see all the influencers influencing the dead internet. MP3 and PNG are of a bygone era: static content was decimated sometime around covid. the future of content is HTML because HTML is a better substrate for ideas in the age of LLMs than any other format. it is a way for humans to actually use computers to improve and layer ideas and if you are not HTML maxxing you are behind. the future is HTML, the future is HTML. HTML as format of tomorrow. HTML as personalized software, perhaps of only single use. HTML as resistance to passive media, from the soma of the scroll. 

viva HTML. viva new ways to explain things we all understand but do not know yet how to package.

Assuming this is 100k a year, that brings it down to roughly 8k a month 

If you want to charge $8,000 a month and want them to retain for 12 months then it cannot be small or medium businesses. It has to be mid-market or enterprise companies 

Which means companies that are at least 50 or 100 employees and you'll need a very nice nurture motion and an ABM motion to get them 

And it should ideally also be an absolute focus on a key channel for them and you taking over the entire channel 

Some ideas that come to mind are building a UGC and content motion for a fast-growing AI consumer app , or complete end-to-end content motions from a two-hour-long podcast getting converted into blogs, getting converted into clips, that get converted into short-form videos for Instagram Reels, YouTube Shorts, TikTok, LinkedIn posts, and Twitter posts 

If you can build an Alex Hormuzzi-type system for me, where you take out the valuable key pieces from a long-form video which is high quality, cut them into short-form clips (short-form horizontal clips for YouTube), as well as turn them into short-form videos for social media, as well as turn them into tweets and stuff.
